claims.text: The recorded distances put this trip 1.90 km off the recommended route: actual distance 24.3 km against the recommended 22.4 km, giving a derived deviation of 1.90 km. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation as actual minus recommended distance using the platform's recorded distances, and 1.90 km is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is established and this is not a within-tolerance case.

The driver-device trace independently shows which route was taken: fixes on Loyang Avenue and Loyang Way from 01:38:30 to 01:44:00, off the recommended TPE alignment, with the vehicle rejoining only at Pasir Ris Close at 01:44:03. The trace is complete — 54 fixes at a 30 s interval, 100% coverage, no gap exceeding 30 s — so the deviation is corroborated by the trace as well as by the recorded distances.

Nothing in the record justifies the reroute. The only traffic data is the LTA advisory for the recommended TPE segment, and its type is NONE — it records no incident, roadwork or closure — and the derived assessment sets justifies_reroute to false. POL-RD-23 permits a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure, so the driver's bare assertion of a 'short cut' cannot justify it.

The driver gave the rider no notice before or at the point of deviation as POL-RD-21 requires. The deviation was detected at 01:38:36; the first rider message is at 01:40:46 and the driver's first and only message is at 01:42:36 — 'Relax lah short cut only' — after the deviation and only in reply. The trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so no verbal notice supported by a call recording can be established either.

The rider did not agree to the deviation; she objected to it in real time. Her messages ask where the driver is going and state that this is not the way, and ask him to slow down. POL-RD-21 treats a deviation as agreed only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment, and this chat log records the opposite of acknowledgment.

Row (d) of the POL-RD-24 matrix applies: the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That derived figure is 1.37 SGD — 1.90 km at the recorded per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge applied. It is money owed to the rider out of the 8.00 SGD she contested, so the outcome on the money is a PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03, not NO_ACTION.

The rider's entitlement on the deviation is not blocked by any threshold: the disputed value is 8.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD AI-final line in POL-GEN-22, the driver's fraud_flags is 0 (and an absent fraud flag counts as 0), and the 2 km limb of POL-RD-25 is switched off — ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — while the 1.90 km deviation would sit under it in any event. POL-GEN-26 does not apply here: every fact the matrix needs — distances, route, chat, fare, traffic data — is present and complete.

The dispute is flagged safety-related and the record carries the safety indicators POL-GEN-21 names: the rider wrote 'Please slow down, you are driving very fast and I feel scared', the driver replied 'Relax lah short cut only', and the claim reports being taken off the expressway into a dark area late at night. POL-GEN-21 requires human review whatever category the filer chose; the AI may not determine fault or recommend a resolution on it, and the contested amount is held rather than collected while the reviewer decides — including the rider's request that this driver's conduct be reviewed.

claims.text: This dispute is safety-flagged and the record itself carries a safety indicator: the rider wrote in app 'Please slow down, you are driving very fast and I feel scared' (MSG-05013-002, sent 01:41:36) and the claim asks that the driver be reviewed. Under POL-GEN-21 the case must go to human review whatever category the filer chose, and the AI may gather evidence and prepare the file but may not issue a ruling, determine fault or recommend a resolution on it. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalation is terminal, issues no monetary outcome and holds the amount, so the charged fare of 38.51 SGD with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stands and nothing is returned now. That is the position the driver asks the judge to take.

The rider asks for 8.00 SGD back, but on this record the route-deviation matrix can move only the excess distance fare. The deviation is 1.90 km (recorded actual 24.3 km less optimal 22.4 km, measured as POL-RD-22 directs from the platform's recorded distances) and the per-km rate is 0.72 SGD, giving 1.90 x 0.72 = 1.37 SGD, with no surge applied to the excess inside the formula POL-RD-24 sets out. The metered total of 38.51 SGD, including the 12.54 SGD surge, is therefore not recoverable as a whole, and a FULL_REFUND of the contested amount is not a remedy the policy provides on these facts.

The speeding allegation is not corroborated by any artifact. The driver-device GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issue codes, no gap over the sample interval, and no implausible-speed finding recorded by the pre-pass, so the record carries no policy-grade evidence of excessive or dangerous speed. The same trace shows the vehicle back on the recommended route by 01:44:03 and the trip ending at the booked destination, Pasir Ris Close. A bare assertion of speed cannot ground a monetary outcome against the driver; it is a matter for the human reviewer POL-GEN-21 requires.

Even if the judge were to look past the safety escalation and reach the refund matrix, the row is not clean on this record: the rider objected in app ('Uncle where are you going? This is not the way', MSG-05013-001) and the driver answered in app with a reason ('Relax lah short cut only', MSG-05013-003). POL-RD-24 sends a case that fits no row - its own example being 'informed but the rider objected' - to escalation under POL-GEN-26. On that reading the destination is the same one the driver seeks: the amount is held pending review, not refunded.
